To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the deglycosylation of CF respiratory mucus glycoprotein (CF-RMG) with trifluoromenthanesulfonic acid and alpha-N-acetygalactosaminidases resulted in the production of a polypeptide backbone (deglycosylated CF-RMG, CF-DGM), (2) the polypeptide core was immunologically active as evidenced by the production of over thirty hybridoma clones secreting antibodies to CF-DGM,

1) we produced and characterized monoclonal antibodies against purified deglycoslyated cystic fibrous respiratory mucin; 2) the antibodies were directed to four distinct epitopes of the polypeptidic core; 3) the epitopes recognized by the antibodies were not conformation dependent and were not glycosylation dependent; and 4) the antibodies may prove useful for the elucidation of the structure of the peptidyl backbone of human respiratory mucus.
we have produced and characterized monoclonal antibodies against purified deglycoslylated CF respiratory mucus.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the production, characterization and application of monoclonal antibody to deglycosylate mucin from cystic fibrosis patients.
the development of monoclonal antibody probes for the analysis of human respiratory mucus glycoprotein.

the production of monoclonal antibody (MAb) to deglycosylate mucins (DGM), the purification and characterization of the MAbs, the use of the MAbs for the detection and isolation of cDNA clones coding for the DGM and the development of an ELISA for the quantification of mucins in respiratory secretions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
MAbs 10a, b, c, d, e and 29d and IgM 30e recognize the polypeptide chain of the CF-DGM while MAbs 1a and 1b are directed against the carbohydrate moiety of the CF-DMG.
the MAbs are directed against four distinct epitopes located on the peptidyl core of CF-DGM.
MAbs 29d and30e recognize a single epitope while MAbs 1a, 10d and 10e recognize a single antigenic determinant.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed eight stable hybridoma clones secreting monoclonals antibodies against a given sequence in deglycosylatd cystic fibrosis mucus glycoprotein.

(a) The CF-DGM preparation is suitable for the production of MAbs; (b) The MAbs are useful in the study of structure and functions of human respiratory mucin; (c) The MAbs can be useful for the diagnosis of CF; and (d) The MAbs may be useful as therapeutic agents for the treatment of CF

the use of deglycosylating agents in the purification of glycoproteins and subsequent use of the deglycoslyated proteins in the generation of MAbs is a promising approach in the elucidation of the structure of glycoproteic molecules and for the screening of libraries for clones secreing mucins.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the MAbs may also provide a promising approach for the development of a mucin based diagnostic test for CF.
we were able to produce MAbs to deglycosylate CF respiratory mucin and that these MAbs are useful in the study of the polypeptides backbone of human respiratory mucus glycoprotein.
the MAbs may be used to screen cDNA libraries for the identification of mucin cDNA clones.
